rationale: This is an arithmetic sum of two already-archived numerators (che−dlc from Accrual-Haircut Net Cash Value and the TS_MAX working-capital release from Working-Capital-Reversal Earnings Value) over the identical archived denominator, so it is a cosmetic blend rather than a new mechanism, and mixing a liquidity stock with a one-period flow release dilutes both channels.

Because oancf ≈ ib + dpc − ΔNOWC, the numerator oancf + ΔNOWC − dpc algebraically collapses to roughly net income, making this a rediscovery of plain earnings-to-price dressed in cash-flow language and internally inconsistent with the stated "cash earnings after a depreciation reserve" rationale.

The level-scaled numerator (NOWC + dlc) divided by market value is mechanically a value/leverage ratio that is high for cheap, asset-heavy firms, and the archive's Noncash-Asset Congestion Trap already showed this construct loads with a positive slope, directly contradicting the negative expected sign without any diagnosis of that contradiction.

Stripping the earnings-yield leg leaves the peak-relative working-capital release alone, which is essentially the published working-capital accrual anomaly (low/declining ΔNOWC predicting higher returns) and also the isolated second leg of the archived generation-7 signal, so it is both a known anomaly and a component ablation rather than a new cross-theme interaction.

The refinement retains the archived congestion signal's first leg and replaces the second with (lct−che)/market equity, a liability-to-price ratio that is mechanically high for cheap and levered firms and therefore likely to push the composite toward positive predicted returns, worsening rather than fixing the sign problem it claims to address.

This is a minor variant of the archived Working-Capital-Ex Book Value (dropping the operating-liability add-back) and reduces to a conservative book-to-market/net-asset-value measure, i.e., a well-known value anomaly refinement with no genuine cross-theme interaction.
